controls.title: Designate a data fiduciary accountable for DPDPA compliance
controls.obligation: Every entity that determines the purpose and means of processing digital personal data is a Data Fiduciary and bears primary statutory accountability under Section 8 of the DPDP Act, regardless of contract structure.

evidence_required.description: Board resolution or partnership deed naming the Data Fiduciary entity
Authoritative organisational record (MCA / GST filing) showing the entity

assessment_questions.prompt: Is there a single legal entity formally identified as the Data Fiduciary for the personal data you process?

controls.title: Publish a privacy policy covering all processing activities
controls.obligation: A publicly accessible privacy policy must describe the personal data processed, the purposes, the rights of data principals, and contact information for grievance redressal (Section 5(3) read with Rule 3).

evidence_required.description: Public privacy policy URL with version + effective date
Live screenshot of the published policy

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you have a publicly accessible privacy policy that meets Section 5(3) requirements?
When was the policy last reviewed and is the version date visible on the page?

controls.title: Maintain a written data-processing agreement with every Data Processor
controls.obligation: Personal data may be processed by a Data Processor only under a valid contract that limits processing to the Data Fiduciary's instructions, enforces security safeguards, and binds the processor to the Act (Section 8(1), Rule 6).

evidence_required.description: Signed DPA with each processor covering scope, security, sub-processors, return/deletion

assessment_questions.prompt: List all third parties that process personal data on your behalf (Data Processors).
For each processor, is there a signed DPA that meets Rule 6 requirements?

controls.title: Obtain free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous consent
controls.obligation: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, with a clear affirmative action, and must be capable of being withdrawn as easily as it was given (Section 6(1)–(4)).

evidence_required.description: Screenshot of the consent capture UX showing it is un-bundled and affirmative
Sample of consent records with timestamp and version of notice shown

assessment_questions.prompt: Is consent obtained via a clear affirmative action (not pre-ticked boxes or implied consent)?
Is the consent notice shown at the time of consent and version-pinned?
Can the data principal withdraw consent as easily as they gave it?

controls.title: Issue notice before or alongside consent specifying purpose, items, and rights
controls.obligation: Before seeking consent the Data Fiduciary must issue a notice describing the personal data and the purpose of processing, the manner of exercising rights, and the means of making a complaint (Section 5(1)–(2), Rule 3).

evidence_required.description: Consent notice text showing all required items
Live UI showing notice at point of consent

assessment_questions.prompt: Does the notice describe the personal data items being collected and the specific purpose?
Does the notice explain how to exercise rights and how to make a complaint?

controls.title: Maintain a consent ledger with at least 7-year retention
controls.obligation: Records of consent — including the notice version, the data principal identifier, the timestamp, and the items consented to — must be retained for at least 7 years from the date of consent or last action, whichever is later (Rule 4 read with the First Schedule).

evidence_required.description: Schema + retention policy showing 7-year retention on consent records
Sample consent record with all required fields

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you store a record of every consent with timestamp + notice version + items + data principal ID?
Is the retention period at least 7 years?

controls.title: Honor consent withdrawal and erase related data
controls.obligation: On withdrawal of consent, processing must stop and personal data must be erased within a reasonable time, except where retention is necessary for legal obligation (Section 6(4), 8(7)).

evidence_required.description: Withdrawal workflow showing receipt → action → completion
Policy on what is erased vs retained and why

assessment_questions.prompt: Is there a working mechanism for users to withdraw consent?
After withdrawal, is the user's personal data erased from active systems within a reasonable time?

controls.title: Publish an itemised list of personal data collected for each purpose
controls.obligation: The notice must itemise the personal data being collected and the specific purpose, not generic categories. "Personal data" must be itemised at a level a data principal can understand and consent to specifically.

evidence_required.description: Notice text showing itemised fields

assessment_questions.prompt: For each processing purpose, does the notice itemise the specific data fields collected?

controls.title: Provide a right-of-access mechanism (summary of personal data held)
controls.obligation: A data principal has the right to obtain a summary of their personal data being processed and the related processing activities (Section 11(1), Rule 14).

evidence_required.description: DSAR intake + identity verification flow
Sample of past fulfilled access requests

assessment_questions.prompt: Can a data principal request a copy of their personal data you hold?
Within what timeframe do you respond?

controls.title: Provide right to correction and erasure of personal data
controls.obligation: A data principal may request correction or erasure of their personal data where it is incomplete, inaccurate, or no longer necessary (Section 12, Rule 14).

evidence_required.description: Correction/erasure request workflow
Sample of completed correction/erasure requests

assessment_questions.prompt: Can a data principal request correction of inaccurate personal data?
Can a data principal request erasure of personal data, and do you action it across all systems (including processors)?

controls.title: Operate a grievance redressal mechanism with named contact
controls.obligation: The Data Fiduciary must establish a grievance redressal mechanism and respond to data principal complaints within 30 days, with the name and contact details of the grievance officer published (Section 13(1), Rule 14).

evidence_required.description: Published grievance officer name and contact
Grievance ticketing with response time tracking

assessment_questions.prompt: Is the grievance officer name and contact publicly available?
Do you respond to complaints within 30 days?

controls.title: Provide right to nominate another individual
controls.obligation: A data principal may nominate another individual to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity (Section 14).

evidence_required.description: Nomination feature in user account
Notice describing the right

assessment_questions.prompt: Can a user nominate another individual to exercise their rights?

controls.title: Maintain a Record of Processing Activities (RoPA)
controls.obligation: The Data Fiduciary must maintain accurate and up-to-date records of its processing activities, sufficient to demonstrate compliance (Rule 8 read with the Third Schedule).

evidence_required.description: Living RoPA — purpose, data items, lawful basis, processors, retention, cross-border

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you maintain a written Record of Processing Activities?
Is it updated within 30 days of any change in processing?

controls.title: Capture a complete data inventory (systems, fields, flows)
controls.obligation: The RoPA must be backed by an actual inventory of systems, databases, fields and data flows — not a generic narrative. Records must be available on demand to the Data Protection Board.

evidence_required.description: System-level inventory with field-level personal-data classification

assessment_questions.prompt: Have you inventoried all systems that hold personal data?
Is the inventory field-level (not just system-level)?

controls.title: Notify the Data Protection Board of a personal data breach
controls.obligation: On becoming aware of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary must inform the Data Protection Board and the affected data principals in the manner and within the time prescribed (Section 8(6), Rules 19–20).

evidence_required.description: Breach response runbook with 72-hour DPB clock
Forensic log capture capability

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you have a documented breach response procedure?
Can you meet the statutory notification clock (typically 72 hours from awareness)?
Do you have forensic log capture sufficient to reconstruct a breach?

controls.title: Notify affected data principals of a breach where harm is likely
controls.obligation: Where a breach is likely to cause harm to a data principal, the Data Fiduciary must inform affected principals without delay, in plain language, of the nature of the breach and the protective measures (Rule 7).

evidence_required.description: Principal notification template and trigger criteria

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you have a template for notifying affected principals?
Is the trigger criteria for principal notification defined?

controls.title: Restrict cross-border transfer to countries not on the restricted list
controls.obligation: Personal data may be transferred outside India only to countries or territories not specifically restricted by the Central Government via notification (Section 16, Rule 15).

evidence_required.description: Data flow map showing all cross-border destinations
Policy and DPA clauses restricting transfer to allowed jurisdictions

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you transfer any personal data outside India?
If yes, are all destinations confirmed not on the restricted list (as notified by the Central Government)?

controls.title: Document the legal basis for any cross-border transfer
controls.obligation: Every cross-border transfer must be supported by a specific contract clause, consent, or other lawful basis that meets Section 16 requirements.

evidence_required.description: Transfer impact assessment or contract clauses

assessment_questions.prompt: For each cross-border transfer, is the legal basis documented?

controls.title: Obtain verifiable parental consent before processing children's data
controls.obligation: Personal data of children (under 18) may be processed only with verifiable parental consent, and processing must not be detrimental to the well-being of the child (Section 9, Rule 10).

evidence_required.description: Age-gate + parental consent flow
Age-appropriate notice language

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you process data of children (users under 18)?
If yes, do you obtain verifiable parental consent before processing?

controls.title: Refuse to undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children
controls.obligation: Data Fiduciaries must not undertake tracking, behavioural monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children (Section 9(2), Rule 10).

evidence_required.description: Ad-tech and analytics exclusion for child users
Internal policy on no-targeted-ads-to-children

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you run any tracking, behavioural monitoring, or targeted advertising that could reach children?

controls.title: Appoint a Data Protection Officer (India-based, named)
controls.obligation: A Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India who reports to the board, and publish their name and contact (Section 10, Rule 13).

evidence_required.description: DPO appointment letter, India-based address, board reporting line
Public DPO contact on website

assessment_questions.prompt: Have you been designated as a Significant Data Fiduciary by the Central Government?
If yes, have you appointed a Data Protection Officer based in India and published their contact?

controls.title: Conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA)
controls.obligation: A Significant Data Fiduciary must conduct periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments, including for any processing that is likely to cause harm to a data principal (Section 10, Rule 13).

evidence_required.description: DPIA template + completed DPIA artifacts

assessment_questions.prompt: Are DPIAs conducted at least annually, and prior to any new high-risk processing?

controls.title: Submit to periodic audit by an independent Data Auditor
controls.obligation: A Significant Data Fiduciary must be audited periodically by an independent Data Auditor, and the audit report must be submitted to the Board (Section 10, Rule 13).

evidence_required.description: Independent audit engagement + latest audit report

assessment_questions.prompt: Are you audited annually by an independent Data Auditor?

controls.title: Implement reasonable security safeguards (technical + organisational)
controls.obligation: The Data Fiduciary must protect personal data in its possession by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach (Section 8(5)). Failure constitutes grounds for the highest penalty tier under Section 33(7).

evidence_required.description: Encryption at rest + in transit, access controls, MFA, logging
Security policy + incident response plan

assessment_questions.prompt: Is personal data encrypted at rest (AES-256 or equivalent) and in transit (TLS 1.2+)?
Is multi-factor authentication enforced for administrative access to personal data stores?
Is access to personal data logged and reviewed?

controls.title: Enforce least-privilege access to personal data
controls.obligation: Access to personal data must be limited to personnel who require it for the documented purpose, with role-based access controls and periodic access review.

evidence_required.description: RBAC configuration + access review logs

assessment_questions.prompt: Is access to personal data gated by role-based access control?
Are access rights reviewed at least annually?

controls.title: Maintain audit logs of access and processing of personal data
controls.obligation: Comprehensive, tamper-evident logs of who accessed or processed personal data, when, and for what purpose must be maintained for forensic and regulatory use.

evidence_required.description: Append-only, hash-chained audit ledger

assessment_questions.prompt: Are all access and processing events recorded to an append-only audit log?
Is the log tamper-evident (e.g. hash-chained, write-once)?

controls.title: Conduct periodic vulnerability assessment and penetration testing
controls.obligation: Personal-data-bearing systems should be subject to periodic vulnerability assessment and penetration testing, with findings remediated within a defined SLA.

evidence_required.description: Latest VAPT report + remediation evidence

assessment_questions.prompt: When was your last VAPT?

controls.title: Encrypt backups of personal data
controls.obligation: Backups containing personal data must be encrypted and access-controlled at the same standard as the primary system.

evidence_required.description: Backup encryption configuration

assessment_questions.prompt: Are backups encrypted at rest?

controls.title: Define and enforce a retention schedule for personal data
controls.obligation: Personal data must be retained only for as long as necessary to satisfy the purpose for which it was collected, and erased thereafter (Section 8(7)).

evidence_required.description: Written retention schedule with purpose-linked durations
System-level enforcement of retention + deletion

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you have a written retention schedule for each category of personal data?
Is retention enforced automatically in your systems?

controls.title: Erase personal data upon purpose-end or withdrawal
controls.obligation: On the conclusion of the processing purpose, or on consent withdrawal, the Data Fiduciary must erase the personal data unless retention is required for legal obligation (Section 8(7)).

evidence_required.description: Erasure workflow + sample completed erasures

assessment_questions.prompt: Is erasure performed on the documented trigger (purpose end / withdrawal / retention expiry)?

controls.title: Maintain an exception register for legally-required retention
controls.obligation: Where erasure is deferred for a legal obligation (e.g. tax, AML, litigation hold), the basis, scope, and the responsible officer must be recorded in a register that an auditor or the Board can review.

evidence_required.description: Exception register with reason, scope, owner, expiry

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you maintain a register of records retained for legal obligation rather than erased?

controls.title: Publish contact details for privacy inquiries
controls.obligation: An email and a contact mechanism for privacy inquiries must be publicly available; this can be a grievance officer or a DPO depending on the entity's SDF status.

evidence_required.description: Public contact details

assessment_questions.prompt: Is a privacy contact email publicly listed?

controls.title: Designate a single point of accountability for privacy
controls.obligation: Even non-SDF Data Fiduciaries benefit from designating a single internal owner — typically a Privacy Lead — who is responsible for the privacy programme, escalation, and Board reporting.

evidence_required.description: Internal appointment / role description

assessment_questions.prompt: Is there a named individual accountable for the privacy programme?

controls.title: Maintain a continuous, timestamped evidence history of compliance
controls.obligation: A defensible compliance posture requires a continuous, timestamped, tamper-evident history of compliance evidence — not point-in-time documentation. This is the operational manifestation of the Act's "demonstrate compliance" burden.

evidence_required.description: Append-only, hash-chained evidence ledger spanning the assessment period

assessment_questions.prompt: Can you produce, on demand, a verifiable, timestamped history of every compliance control for the past 12 months?

controls.title: Report posture to the Board or Audit Committee at least annually
controls.obligation: A periodic (at least annual) posture report to the Board or Audit Committee establishes governance accountability and provides defensible evidence of oversight.

evidence_required.description: Most recent Board / Audit Committee privacy report

assessment_questions.prompt: Has the Board / Audit Committee received a privacy posture update in the past 12 months?

controls.title: Conduct a DPIA before launching any new high-risk processing
controls.obligation: Where processing is likely to cause harm to data principals — large-scale profiling, biometric processing, children, cross-border — a Data Protection Impact Assessment must be completed before processing begins.

evidence_required.description: DPIA template + completed DPIAs for high-risk processing

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you conduct a DPIA before any new high-risk processing?

controls.title: Capture and remediate risks identified in the DPIA
controls.obligation: Risks identified in a DPIA must be tracked to closure with an owner, a remediation plan, and a re-assessment after remediation.

evidence_required.description: DPIA risk register + closure evidence

assessment_questions.prompt: Are DPIA findings tracked in a risk register with owners and closure dates?

controls.title: Maintain a current org chart of data processing responsibilities
controls.obligation: Roles and responsibilities for privacy must be visible and current — who decides purposes, who signs off on processors, who handles DSARs, who is on the breach call.

evidence_required.description: RACI / org chart for privacy

assessment_questions.prompt: Is there a current RACI or org chart for privacy responsibilities?

controls.title: Conduct annual privacy training for staff handling personal data
controls.obligation: Personnel handling personal data must receive privacy training on induction and at least annually thereafter, with completion recorded.

evidence_required.description: Training records with completion status

assessment_questions.prompt: Do all staff handling personal data receive annual privacy training?

controls.title: Designate a breach response owner with a documented playbook
controls.obligation: A named individual must own breach response end-to-end, with a documented playbook covering detection → triage → notification → post-mortem, exercised at least annually.

evidence_required.description: Breach response playbook
Tabletop exercise record

assessment_questions.prompt: Is there a named breach response owner and a current playbook?
Has a tabletop exercise been run in the past 12 months?

controls.title: Map and document data flows to processors and sub-processors
controls.obligation: Beyond the RoPA, a working data-flow map (system-of-systems diagram) showing personal data movement — including to sub-processors — must be available for the Board and any DPB inquiry.

evidence_required.description: Data flow diagram with processors and sub-processors

assessment_questions.prompt: Is there a current data-flow map showing processors and sub-processors?

controls.title: Conduct a transfer impact assessment for high-risk destinations
controls.obligation: For transfers to jurisdictions with materially different data protection regimes, a transfer impact assessment should be completed to demonstrate that the receiving environment provides comparable protection.

evidence_required.description: TIA per high-risk destination

assessment_questions.prompt: Have you completed a transfer impact assessment for each cross-border destination with weaker protection?

controls.title: Securely dispose of media and devices containing personal data
controls.obligation: Media and devices containing personal data, including at end-of-life, must be securely wiped or destroyed with a documented process and certificate of destruction where applicable.

evidence_required.description: Media sanitisation policy + certificate of destruction register

assessment_questions.prompt: Is there a documented media sanitisation process and a register of end-of-life destructions?

controls.title: Operate an incident response capability with rehearsed playbook
controls.obligation: Beyond breach notification, an operational incident response capability — on-call, escalation, runbook, post-mortem — is necessary to meet the 72-hour clock in practice, not just in policy.

evidence_required.description: Incident response runbook + on-call roster
Tabletop exercise record

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you have an on-call rotation and runbook for security incidents?

controls.title: Verify the identity of a data principal before acting on rights requests
controls.obligation: Identity verification proportional to the sensitivity of the request is required before acting on access, correction, or erasure requests, to prevent unauthorised disclosure.

evidence_required.description: Identity verification procedure

assessment_questions.prompt: Do you verify the identity of the data principal before fulfilling rights requests?

controls.title: Provide data portability in a structured, commonly used format
controls.obligation: On request, the data principal is entitled to receive a copy of their personal data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format (Section 11(2)).

evidence_required.description: Export pipeline producing JSON / CSV in a documented schema

assessment_questions.prompt: Can you export a user's data in a structured, machine-readable format on request?

frameworks.title: Master Direction on Information Technology Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices
frameworks.description: RBI direction to supervised entities on board-level IT governance, information security controls, IS audit and resilience. The BFSI sector's broadest baseline IT/data regime.
frameworks.notes: Reference record. Chapter-level topical refs only; paragraph-level mapping and verbatim verification against the printed Master Direction are pending.

frameworks.title: Master Direction on Non-Banking Financial Company – Account Aggregator (consent-artefact regime)
frameworks.description: The Account Aggregator regime's consent-artefact model: explicit, purpose-bound, revocable consent before financial information is fetched or shared. The plan's named "RBI / Account Aggregator overlay" for pack #1.
frameworks.notes: Reference record. The consent-artefact obligations are topical refs; the printed Direction and its amendments must be re-verified before any equivalence claim.

frameworks.title: Directive on Storage of Payment System Data
frameworks.description: Payment system data must be stored only in India; any processing abroad is time-bound with erasure obligations. Strictly stricter than the DPDPA's cross-border blacklist model.

frameworks.title: SEBI Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework for regulated entities
frameworks.description: Baseline cyber-security controls, monitoring, VAPT and time-bound incident reporting for SEBI-regulated market intermediaries.
frameworks.notes: Reference record; circular-level citation and clause verification pending.

frameworks.title: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines
frameworks.description: Information-security baseline, access and audit-logging, and outsourcing oversight for insurers carrying policyholder data.
frameworks.notes: Reference record; the guideline edition in force for a given insurer must be confirmed during engagement, not assumed.

frameworks.title: Directions under section 70B(6) of the Information Technology Act, 2000
frameworks.description: Six-hour incident reporting to CERT-In and a rolling 180-day in-India log retention for all ICT systems — cross-sector, but unavoidable in BFSI.
frameworks.notes: Reference record; the Directions are public and clause refs are slugs pending verification.

framework_controls.heading: Board-approved IT governance and risk-management oversight
Information security controls protecting financial-sector systems and data
Explicit, purpose-bound, revocable consent artefact before financial information is fetched or shared
Need-based collection; no storage of financial information beyond the consented purpose
Grievance redressal and data-access obligations for AA ecosystem participants
End-to-end payment system data stored only in India
Processing abroad, where permitted, is time-bound with erasure obligations
Baseline cyber-security controls with defined governance and board oversight
Continuous monitoring, audit logging and periodic VAPT of market-facing systems
Time-bound reporting of cyber incidents to SEBI and CERT-In
Information security baseline for systems holding policyholder data
Access control, privileged access management and audit logging
Oversight of outsourced and cloud arrangements processing policyholder data
Report specified cyber incidents to CERT-In within six hours of noticing
Retain ICT system logs for a rolling 180 days, within India

control_mappings.note: Both regimes demand board-level accountability — the MD for IT risk, DPDPA s.8 for personal-data fiduciary accountability. Overlap is real but the scopes differ; not an equivalence claim.
The MD's baseline information-security controls satisfy much of DPDPA s.8(5) "reasonable security" for a supervised entity, but the MD adds regulator-specific duties DPDPA does not.
An IS audit evidences continuous compliance practice; the DPDPA control wants a timestamped evidence history. A starting point for the coverage map, not a claim.
The AA consent artefact is domain-specific and stricter in shape (structured, signed, revocable) than generic DPDPA consent; satisfying AA does not exhaust s.6, and vice versa.
The artefact's purpose declaration parallels the DPDPA notice's itemised purposes; the mapping needs engagement-level confirmation.
No-storage-beyond-the-consented-purpose parallels erasure on purpose-end. Directionally aligned; the clocks and scope differ.
AA grievance duties overlap the DPDPA grievance-redressal mechanism for fiduciaries in the AA ecosystem.
Both restrict cross-border flows, but the RBI directive localises payment data outright — strictly stricter than the DPDPA blacklist model. The overlap is real; the obligations are not the same.
Documenting the legal basis for a transfer parallels documenting the time-bound foreign-processing window; the mapping informs the coverage map only.
Baseline cyber controls overlap "reasonable security safeguards" for SEBI-regulated entities; the framework adds market-integrity duties outside DPDPA scope.
Framework monitoring/logging duties satisfy much of the DPDPA audit-log control for market-facing systems; scope and retention specifics differ.
Periodic VAPT appears in both; cadence and scoping must be confirmed per engagement before any stronger label.
Both are time-bound breach/incident intimation duties with DIFFERENT recipients and clocks (SEBI/CERT-In vs the Data Protection Board). One report does not substitute for the other.
The insurer information-security baseline overlaps reasonable security for policyholder data; the guideline edition in force must be confirmed per engagement.
Privileged access management overlaps DPDPA least-privilege access; the mapping informs, it does not equate.
Outsourcing oversight overlaps the DPDPA processor-agreement control; the DPA remains a distinct statutory requirement.
The 6-hour CERT-In clock is stricter than and separate from the DPB intimation duty — different authority, different trigger. Never present one as satisfying the other.
The Directions mandate a rolling 180-day in-India log retention that exceeds what the DPDPA audit-log control alone requires.
Log-retention schedules must be reconciled so the CERT-In minimum and DPDPA erasure duties do not collide in the retention register.

packs.name: BFSI sector pack #1 — banking, financial services and insurance
packs.description: Overlay of the plan-named financial-sector regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI) plus CERT-In onto the DPDPA control set, per M4.2/M4.8. Pack #1 per the operator decision of 2026-09-26 (pack order BFSI → Healthcare → Tech/E-commerce).

evidence_requirements.requirement: Regulator-grade IS audit or CERT-In-empanelled auditor summary covering the assessment window
Board or audit-committee minutes evidencing IT and privacy governance oversight
Sample consent artefacts (AA ecosystem) reconciled against the consent ledger
Incident register showing regulator intimation timelines (CERT-In 6-hour clock; DPB intimation) kept distinct

packs.basis: Reference pack: derived from the regulators' public materials, with topical framework-control slugs and mapping strengths capped at partial. No mapping claims equivalence, and nothing is vendor-verified — that requires client tenants.
